treeshapesim

Simulate rooted, binary, ultrametric trees in which topological imbalance and the distribution of branching times are set by separate parameters.

  • Topology: Aldous’ (1996) beta-splitting model. beta = 0 gives Yule trees, lower values give more imbalanced trees and higher values more balanced ones.
  • Branching times: a pure-birth process in which each of the k lineages splits at rate k^c. c = 0 is Yule, c < 0 slows diversification towards the present (negative gamma; Pybus & Harvey, 2000) and c > 0 speeds it up.

The gamma statistic depends only on the internode intervals and the Colless index only on the topology, so beta mainly moves the Colless index and c mainly moves gamma.

Documentation: https://provetelab.org/treeshapesim/

Installation 

install.packages("treeshapesim", repos = c("https://diogoprov.r-universe.dev",
                                           "https://cloud.r-project.org"))
# or
remotes::install_github("diogoprov/treeshapesim")

Example 

library(treeshapesim)
set.seed(1)
tr <- sim_tree_shape(100, beta = -1, c = -0.5)   # imbalanced, early splits
tree_shape(tr)                                    # gamma and normalized Colless

# trees near target values of gamma and Colless
cal <- calibrate_shape(100)                       # calibration for 100 tips
trees <- sim_tree_target(100, gamma = -2, colless = 1, nsim = 50, tol = 0.25,
                         calibration = cal)

# a 3 x 3 grid of tree shapes and the parameters of each cell
grid <- shape_grid(100, gamma = c(-2, -1, 0), colless = c(0, 0.5, 1),
                   calibration = cal)

# any other dependence of the split rate on the number of lineages
tr <- sim_tree_shape(100, rate = function(k) 1 - k / 110)   # logistic

See vignette("treeshapesim") for a walk-through. Many other tree statistics can be computed with treestats.

Use with comdynamite

treeshapesim produces the regional species pools of comdynamite, which simulates process-based metacommunities with phylogenetic structure. The two packages split the work: treeshapesim sets the shape of the tree, and comdynamite takes that tree as a fixed input, places traits on it with a chosen phylogenetic signal and runs the community dynamics. Any phylo object from sim_tree_shape() or sim_tree_target() can be passed directly as the species argument of comdynamite, so tree shape, phylogenetic signal and dispersal can be varied as separate factors in a simulation study. Neither package depends on the other.

# remotes::install_github("diogoprov/comdynamite")
library(comdynamite)
set.seed(1)
pool <- sim_tree_shape(40, beta = -1, c = -0.5)    # imbalanced, early splits
sim <- simulate_metacommunity(
  landscape = landscape_implicit(20),
  traits    = species_traits(pool, lambda = 1),
  alpha     = competition_matrix(pool, type = "phylo"),
  dispersal = 0.01,
  n_steps   = 1000
)
sim$abundance                                      # sites x species

To replicate across shapes, shape_grid() gives beta and c for each combination of gamma and Colless, and sim_tree_target() draws the pools of each cell.

prune_tips() removes a fraction of the pool before the simulation, at random, in clusters on the tree or according to a trait, to ask how the pattern of extinction changes the communities. The article Tree shape and extinction in metacommunity simulations with comdynamite works through a factorial design.

How treeshapesim differs from TreeSim, TreeSimGM and apTreeshape

treeshapesim TreeSim TreeSimGM apTreeshape
Purpose Trees whose imbalance and distribution of branching times vary independently, for simulation studies on tree shape Trees from birth–death processes Trees from a general Bellman–Harris model of speciation and extinction, with lineage-specific shifts Analysis and simulation of tree topologies
Topology Aldous’ beta-splitting model, with beta as a continuous parameter Not a parameter: it follows from the birth–death process Not a parameter: it follows from the waiting times, the speciation mode (symmetric or asymmetric) and the shifts Yule, PDA, Aldous’ branching, biased and user-defined split models (rtreeshape()); beta-splitting with a clade age–richness index (simulate_tree(), simulate_yule())
Branching times Pure birth with per-lineage rate k^c or any function of k (rate), drawn independently of the topology, so gamma can be negative, near zero or positive Birth–death with constant rates, rate shifts, mass extinctions or density-dependent speciation, conditioned on the number of tips and/or the age Any distribution of the waiting times to speciation and to extinction (for instance, age-dependent), rescaled in lineages with shifts; conditioned on the number of tips (sim.taxa(), optionally with GSA) or the age (sim.age()) None (rtreeshape()), ranks 1 to n − 1 (simulate_tree()) or a constant-rate birth–death process (simulate_yule())
Separate control of imbalance and branching times Yes: the realized gamma depends only on c and the realized Colless index only on beta No: imbalance is not set No: one process produces both Imbalance is set by beta; branching times have no shape parameter of their own
Target values of gamma and Colless Yes: calibration, rejection to a tolerance and grids of shapes (sim_tree_target(), shape_grid()) No No No
Extinction, serial sampling, gene trees No (pure birth), but random incomplete sampling of tips (sampling_fraction) and one extinction event at the tips, random or not (prune_tips()) Yes Extinction, with or without the extinct lineages (complete), and incomplete sampling, at random or in proportion to pendant branch lengths; no serial sampling or gene trees Extinction in the ranked-tree models
Estimation and tests of tree shape Estimation of beta and c from an empirical tree, with a parametric bootstrap (fit_shape()); no tests No No Yes (e.g. maxlik.betasplit(), aldous.test())

Use TreeSim for trees from specific birth–death models, TreeSimGM for models with other waiting-time distributions or with speciation and extinction rates that shift between lineages (Hagen & Stadler 2018), and apTreeshape to model, estimate or test topological imbalance. In TreeSim and TreeSimGM the shape of the tree is an outcome of the diversification model, so imbalance and branching times change together. Use treeshapesim when the imbalance and the distribution of branching times have to be varied as separate factors. The comparison is based on the documentation of TreeSim 2.4, TreeSimGM 2.5 and apTreeshape 1.5-0.1; apTreeshape was archived on CRAN in 2023 and is available from the CRAN archive.

Hagen, O., & Stadler, T. (2018). TreeSimGM: Simulating phylogenetic trees under general Bellman–Harris models with lineage-specific shifts of speciation and extinction in R. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 9, 754–760. https://doi.org/10.1111/2041-210X.12917

Citation

Provete, D. B. (2026). treeshapesim: Simulate trees with separately controlled imbalance and branching times. R package. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23647260

This DOI always points to the latest version; each release also has its own DOI on Zenodo. In R, citation("treeshapesim") gives the entry with the installed version.
